IHumanLexiconParams.description:
The parameters every row of the lexicon leaves open, by family and by the
row's export name in its namespace: what an author writes in
`registered(row, params)`, read from the row's own law type, so a page or
a generator reads the same parameters the checker does. A row's fixed
parameters are not among them. A row is registered under its law's
`name`, which a type cannot read, so a reader that wants rows by name
(`HUMAN_LEXICON_SCHEMAS`) pairs each export with its law at run time.

It is derived from `HUMAN_LEXICON_FAMILIES`: each family namespace's
members that plan, keyed by their export name, each with the parameters
its `plan` takes.

AutoMovieHumanoidRegion.description:
Closed vocabulary of anatomical surface regions on a humanoid body: the
places another body or an object touches, strikes, grips or presents to.

Names follow surface anatomy (Gray's Anatomy surface landmarks; the region
divisions of anatomical charts): head and face, neck, the anterior and
posterior trunk with the hypochondriac regions over the liver (right) and
spleen (left) and the lumbar regions over the kidneys, and the limbs by
segment and aspect. Paired regions carry their side, the body's own left
or right. Contact points the body itself presents (the palm, the index
fingertip, the sole, the heel, the seat) are regions too, so another body
or an object can be aimed at them. Each region is anchored to one humanoid bone and resolved to a
point and an outward normal on that bone's collision shapes by the engine,
so the same name serves a generated Human, an imported character or a
parametric figure. The list grows additively; no name is ever repurposed.

x.description: X: toward the left (+) of a character facing +Z, its right (−).

z.description: Z: the front (+) of a character at zero heading, its back (−).

IAutoMovieVector3.description:
A 3D vector in automovie's right-handed, y-up frame, as in glTF 2.0 and VRM 1.0.

The same shape carries metre positions/translations, unitless directions and per-axis factors such as scale. The containing field states its meaning and required range; this type enforces neither finiteness nor length, which remain the owning record's admission responsibility.

AutoMovieMotionTarget.description:
What a directed action aims at: another person's anatomical region, a
region of the performer's own body, a named point on a prop, a free point,
or nothing at all.

- `person`: a region of another subject's body; the action commits to its
  position at its commit event and tracks it afterwards.
- `self`: a region of the performer's own body (a hand to the chin, to the
  hip, to the chest), read on the posture the performer is in.
- `prop`: a named point of a prop (a bag's centre, a pad's face, a
  handle), as the prop's profile declares it.
- `point`: a fixed point in metres, in the world or in the performer's own
  frame (+Z forward, +X left, +Y up, origin on the floor under the root).
  Its `normal` says which way the surface at the point faces (a table top
  faces up, a wall faces the room); without one the point faces back at the
  performer.
- `none`: shadow work and drills in the air; the aim point is that of a
  virtual opponent of the performer's own measure at `range` metres
  (default: the technique's own range), at the `line` height (default
  `middle`), so contact checks become extension checks.

rising.description:
A rising trot: the mount's stride time, seconds, or the cue track of
the performance that holds its strides (the footfalls of one
diagonal, as the mount's own ride publishes them). The rider stands
in the stirrups and sits again once a stride, the seat rising `POST`
thigh lengths off the saddle, so both feet must rest on the support.
On a cue track the seat is down at each of its instants and seated
before the first and after the last. Seated throughout when absent.

feet.description:
The support's point each foot stays on, by its id, for a part that
moves within the support: a pedal on its turning crank, a stirrup on
a trotting horse (`IHumanProp.point`). The foot keeps the place it
had on that point when the ride began. A foot not named, or a point
that only moves with the support, is carried rigidly.

seat.description:
The support's point the seat stays on, by its id, where the seat
itself moves within the support: a saddle on a horse's trunk, which
rises and falls with the stride over the course its root follows.
The body is carried with the support alone when absent.

hands.description:
The support's point each hand holds, by its id: a handlebar grip, a
rein, a wheel's rim. The hand goes to it over `TAKE` seconds from the
ride's start and stays on it, following a part that moves within the
support. The arms are still yielded, so an arm action over the ride
takes a hand off for as long as it lasts. The hand turns to the
point and closes on it (`HumanMountRider.hold`).
